question.text: Can an investor stop or modify a running SIP?

answer.text: Yes, the investor can stop, pause, or modify the SIP amount at any time by giving instructions to the fund house
No, once started, SIP cannot be stopped until the end of the committed period
SIP can only be stopped if the investor pays a penalty
Only SEBI can authorize stopping of a SIP

explanation.text: The Logic: A Systematic Investment Plan is an instruction to debit the bank account periodically; it is not a binding contract that locks the investor in for a tenure. Investors retain operational flexibility to stop, pause, increase or decrease the SIP at any time by submitting the appropriate instruction (online or in writing) to the fund house, subject to standard processing lead time before the next instalment date. The Trap: "Cannot be stopped until the end of the committed period" misreads the stated SIP tenure as a hard lock-in; it is an intended duration, not a commitment. "Stopped only with a penalty" is incorrect — there is no penalty for stopping a regular SIP. "Only SEBI can authorize stopping" inserts a regulator approval that is not required for a routine investor instruction. Note: The cited NISM Series V-B workbook pages (171, 172) support SIP enrolment details and top-up / increase facilities but do not explicitly state that a running SIP can be stopped, paused, or modified at any time. The framing above reflects general industry practice for SIP operations at AMCs.
